newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Jakarta stocks seen mixed ahead elections.
newsitem.headline: Jakarta stocks seen mixed ahead elections.

text.p: Jakarta stocks are expected to be mixed on Monday as investors remain concerned over developments ahead of the May 29 general election, brokers said.
"Although there is no more campaigning before the polling day, investors remain concerned, particularly over the riot in Banjarmasin at the weekend," a foreign broker said.
On Monday, Banjarmasin newspaper Dinamika Berita reported that the death toll from a shopping centre fire and riot in the South Kalimantan city had risen to 142.
Brokers said the incident would put some pressure on the market.
Brokers expected trading to be slow as the market was also devoid of fresh corporate news.
"Minor buying will appear on some blue chip stocks as their prices are already at bargain levels," one broker with joint-venture firm said.
Cement maker Semen Gresik and cigarette firm Sampoerna were expected to be among the targets of bargain hunters, he said.
On Friday, the Jakarta composite index closed 4.43 points higher at 658.52 points, against last week's close of 657.07 points.

The campaign for the country's general elections ended on Friday with polling day set for Thursday. Despite tensions because of violence during the campaign, the cooling-off period had given investors some confidence to start picking up blue chip stocks in anticipation that the market would rise after the polls, an analyst with a large local brokerage firm said.

"Despite all the violence and rioting during the campaign period, in general .. the index is moving in our expected range of 640 to 660 points. So there is nothing to worry about, we just need to wait until the election is over," she added.
Brokers ascribed the sluggish market to Friday's riot in Banjarmasin, a city in South Kalimantan on Borneo island, but said the impact was minor as the city is far away from Jakarta.
Cement maker Semen Gresik was also a target of bargain hunters despite announcing lower-than-expected first quarter earnings last Friday, brokers said.

Small property firm Mas Murni Indonesia was the most active stock, rising 25 rupiah to 900 on 3.6 million shares on what brokers said was due to revived speculation of a possible take-over and rights issue.
